# Settings

<!-- Generated by docs/generate.sh from `pub config settings --markdown`; don't edit by hand. -->

Every setting pub understands. Set them in a config file, in a URL query, or with
`-O key=value` (see [Configuration](../configuration.md)). Types: a *duration* is `10s`,
`500ms`, `2m` or `1h` (`0` = none); a *size* is `65536`, `256k`, `4m` or `1g`.

## All protocols

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | string | – | login name (also taken from the URL) |
| `username` | string | – | same as `user` |
| `password` | secret | – | password (also taken from the URL); prefer password-env |
| `password-file` | path | – | file holding the password; must be yours and mode 0400 (see core.config.secret-file-*) |
| `password-env` | string | – | name of an environment variable holding the password |
| `password-prompt` | bool | `false` | ask for the password on the terminal when none is configured (-u user always asks) |
| `destination` | string | – | default destination when the target has no path |
| `tcp-nodelay` | bool | `true` | disable Nagle's algorithm |
| `tcp-keepalive` | bool | `true` | send keepalive probes on idle connections |
| `tcp-keepalive-time` | duration | `30s` | idle time before the first probe; 0 = OS default |
| `tcp-keepalive-interval` | duration | `10s` | time between unanswered probes; 0 = OS default |
| `tcp-keepalive-count` | count | `3` | unanswered probes before the connection is dropped; 0 = OS default |
| `receive-buffer` | size | – | SO_RCVBUF; unset = OS autotuning (setting it disables autotuning) |
| `send-buffer` | size | – | SO_SNDBUF; unset = OS autotuning (setting it disables autotuning) |
| `max-frame-size` | size | `64m` | largest frame accepted from the server; larger ones are a protocol error |
| `max-payload` | size | `64m` | largest message body read from -d, -f or stdin |
| `max-headers` | count | `256` | most headers + properties per message (and subscription headers) |
| `max-header-value` | size | `64k` | largest header or property value |
| `connect-timeout` | duration | `5s` | TCP connect and TLS handshake; 0 = none |
| `send-timeout` | duration | `10s` | a blocked socket write; 0 = none |
| `receive-timeout` | duration | `10s` | an expected server reply (handshake, receipt); 0 = none |
| `tls` | bool | `false` | use TLS even if the scheme does not require it |
| `insecure` | bool | `false` | skip TLS certificate verification |
| `ca-file` | path | – | CA certificates (PEM) to trust instead of the system's |
| `cert` | path | – | client certificate (PEM) for mutual TLS |
| `key` | path | – | client private key (PEM) for mutual TLS |
| `tls-min-version` | tls-version | `1.3` | lowest TLS version to accept (1.2 or 1.3); set 1.2 per host for older brokers |
| `tls-max-version` | tls-version | `1.3` | highest TLS version to offer |
| `tls-cipher-suites` | suite-list | – | allowed cipher suites in preference order; unset = library default (see `pub config settings`) |
| `tls-groups` | group-list | – | key exchange groups in preference order, e.g. X25519,secp256r1; unset = library default |
| `header-strategy` | string | `default` | how send treats headers of messages read from a document (-F json): default (new id, timestamp, ttl from now) or administrative (exact id, timestamp, expiration) |
| `format` | string | `raw` | message format for receive output and send input (`pub formats` lists them; also -F) |
| `message-type` | choice | `bytes` | body type to send: text (must be UTF-8) or bytes; set per module with [module "&lt;name&gt;"] |
| `server-spiffe-id` | spiffe-id | – | verify the server by SPIFFE ID (spiffe://domain/path, or spiffe://domain/* for any workload) against ca-file, instead of by hostname |
| `server-name` | string | – | TLS server name (SNI) if it differs from the host |

## stomp module

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vhost` | string | – | CONNECT `host` header (virtual host); defaults to the URL host |
| `client-id` | string | – | CONNECT `client-id` header, for durable subscriptions |
| `receipts` | bool | `true` | request a RECEIPT for each SEND and wait for it |
| `heart-beat` | duration | `10s` | heart-beat interval offered both ways (STOMP 1.1+); pub fails if the broker goes silent for two (0 = off) |

Destination options, passed through to the broker:

| Option | Applies to | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `activemq.*` | receive | ActiveMQ consumer options, e.g. activemq.prefetchSize, activemq.exclusive |
| `prefetch-count` | receive | RabbitMQ consumer prefetch |
| `x-*` | send+receive | RabbitMQ queue arguments for auto-declared queues, e.g. x-queue-type, x-max-length |

## mqtt module

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | choice | `5` | MQTT protocol version: 5 or 3.1.1 (3.1.1 carries no properties, content-type, correlation-id or ttl) |
| `qos` | choice | `1` | 0 = at most once, 1 = at least once (PUBACK), 2 = exactly once; for send and subscribe |
| `retain` | bool | `false` | ask the broker to keep the message for future subscribers |
| `retain-handling` | choice | `0` | retained messages on subscribe: 0 = send, 1 = only for a new subscription, 2 = don't send |
| `clean-start` | bool | `true` | start a new session; false resumes one (needs client-id) |
| `session-expiry` | duration | `0` | how long the broker keeps the session after disconnect (MQTT 5; --durable: forever) |
| `keep-alive` | duration | `60s` | MQTT keep-alive; pub pings while waiting and fails if the broker stops answering (0 = off) |
| `will-topic` | string | – | a will message: the broker publishes it to this topic if pub's connection ends without a normal DISCONNECT |
| `will-message` | string | `` | the will message's body |
| `will-qos` | choice | `0` | the will message's QoS |
| `will-retain` | bool | `false` | publish the will message as retained |
| `will-delay` | duration | `0` | MQTT 5: wait this long after the connection ends before publishing the will (no will if the session resumes first) |
| `will-on-disconnect` | bool | `false` | MQTT 5: publish the will even when pub disconnects normally |
| `share-group` | string | – | receive through a shared subscription ($share/GROUP/filter): each message goes to one member of the group |
| `topic-aliases` | bool | `true` | MQTT 5: send repeated topics as topic aliases when the broker allows them |
| `topic-alias-maximum` | count | `16` | MQTT 5: how many topic aliases the broker may use when sending to pub (0 = none, at most 1024) |
| `client-id` | string | – | MQTT client identifier; empty lets the broker assign one |

## openwire module

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client-id` | string | – | JMS client ID (jms.clientID); default: generated per connection |
| `client-id-prefix` | string | – | prefix for generated client IDs, as Java's clientIDPrefix: &lt;prefix&gt;-&lt;pid&gt;-&lt;start ms&gt;-0:&lt;n&gt; (ignored when client-id is set) |
| `connection-id-prefix` | string | – | prefix for connection IDs, as Java's connectionIDPrefix: &lt;prefix&gt;-&lt;pid&gt;-&lt;start ms&gt;-1:&lt;n&gt; (producer and message IDs start with it) |
| `wireFormat.tightEncodingEnabled` | bool | `true` | prefer the compact tight encoding; used when the broker agrees |
| `wireFormat.stackTraceEnabled` | bool | `false` | ask for Java stack traces in broker errors (Java default: true) |
| `wireFormat.maxInactivityDuration` | count | `30000` | ms of silence before the connection is presumed dead; keep-alives every third of it (0 = off) |
| `wireFormat.maxInactivityDurationInitalDelay` | count | `10000` | ms before the inactivity monitor starts (Java's spelling, 'Inital') |
| `jms.connectResponseTimeout` | count | `0` | ms to wait for the broker to accept the connection (0 = receive-timeout) |
| `jms.closeTimeout` | count | `15000` | ms to wait for the broker to acknowledge close |
| `broker-type` | choice | `auto` | which broker, for destination management: activemq, artemis, or auto = from the broker's id (classic = activemq) |
| `jms.useAsyncSend` | bool | `false` | send persistent messages without waiting for the broker (non-persistent ones always are) |
| `jms.alwaysSyncSend` | bool | `false` | wait for the broker on every send, persistent or not |
| `jms.sendTimeout` | count | `0` | ms to wait for the broker to accept a message; &gt; 0 makes every send synchronous (0 = receive-timeout) |
| `jms.producerWindowSize` | count | `0` | bytes of asynchronous sends allowed unacknowledged (0 = no producer flow control) |
| `jms.useCompression` | bool | `false` | deflate message bodies (any ActiveMQ client inflates them) |
| `jms.disableTimeStampsByDefault` | bool | `false` | leave JMSTimestamp unset |
| `prefetch-follows-count` | bool | `true` | without an explicit prefetch, take only as many messages as -n asks for (Java: 1000 queue / 32767 topic) |
| `jms.prefetchPolicy.all` | count | – | prefetch for queues and topics (0 = pull one message at a time) |
| `jms.prefetchPolicy.queuePrefetch` | count | – | queue prefetch (Java default 1000) |
| `jms.prefetchPolicy.topicPrefetch` | count | – | topic prefetch (Java default 32767) |
| `jms.prefetchPolicy.durableTopicPrefetch` | count | – | durable subscription prefetch (Java default 100) |
| `jms.prefetchPolicy.queueBrowserPrefetch` | count | – | browse prefetch (Java default 500) |
| `jms.prefetchPolicy.maximumPendingMessageLimit` | count | `0` | messages a slow topic consumer may fall behind before the broker discards old ones (0 = no limit) |
| `jms.dispatchAsync` | bool | `true` | ask the broker to dispatch asynchronously |
| `jms.exclusiveConsumer` | bool | `false` | ask to be the queue's only consumer |
| `jms.useRetroactiveConsumer` | bool | `false` | topics: also receive recent messages the broker kept (needs a broker recovery policy) |
| `jms.sendAcksAsync` | bool | `true` | acknowledge without waiting for the broker |
| `jms.consumerExpiryCheckEnabled` | bool | `true` | drop messages that expired on the way (acknowledged as expired) |

Other names accepted for pub settings:

| Name | Sets | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `connectionTimeout` | `connect-timeout` | milliseconds |
| `soTimeout` | `receive-timeout` | milliseconds |
| `tcpNoDelay` | `tcp-nodelay` | as is |
| `keepAlive` | `tcp-keepalive` | as is |
| `socketBufferSize` | `receive-buffer`, `send-buffer` | as is |
| `wireFormat.maxFrameSize` | `max-frame-size` | as is |
| `jms.clientID` | `client-id` | as is |
| `jms.clientIDPrefix` | `client-id-prefix` | as is |
| `jms.connectionIDPrefix` | `connection-id-prefix` | as is |
| `jms.userName` | `user` | as is |
| `jms.password` | `password` | as is |

Accepted for compatibility, with no effect in pub:

| Setting | Why |
|---|---|
| `wireFormat.cacheEnabled` | pub never uses the marshal cache |
| `wireFormat.cacheSize` | pub never uses the marshal cache |
| `wireFormat.sizePrefixDisabled` | pub always uses the size prefix |
| `wireFormat.tcpNoDelayEnabled` | use tcpNoDelay / tcp-nodelay |
| `trace` | use -v |
| `jms.watchTopicAdvisories` | pub never subscribes to advisory topics |
| `jms.copyMessageOnSend` | pub sends each message once |
| `jms.statsEnabled` | pub keeps no JMS statistics |
| `jms.objectMessageSerializationDefered` | pub does not send ObjectMessages |
| `jms.optimizedMessageDispatch` | client-side dispatch tuning |
| `jms.useDedicatedTaskRunner` | client-side threading |
| `jms.alwaysSessionAsync` | client-side threading |
| `jms.maxThreadPoolSize` | client-side threading |
| `jms.nestedMapAndListEnabled` | pub does not send MapMessages |
| `jms.checkForDuplicates` | client-side duplicate audit |
| `jms.auditDepth` | client-side duplicate audit |
| `jms.auditMaximumProducerNumber` | client-side duplicate audit |
| `jms.transactedIndividualAck` | pub does not use transactions |
| `jms.nonBlockingRedelivery` | pub does not redeliver locally |
| `jms.rmIdFromConnectionId` | XA only |
| `jms.xaAckMode` | XA only |
| `jms.warnAboutUnstartedConnectionTimeout` | pub starts connections immediately |
| `jms.trustAllPackages` | pub does not deserialize ObjectMessages |
| `jms.trustedPackages` | pub does not deserialize ObjectMessages |
| `jms.redeliveryPolicy.*` | pub does not redeliver locally |
| `jms.blobTransferPolicy.*` | blob messages are not supported |
| `jms.prefetchPolicy.optimizeDurableTopicPrefetch` | pub does not create durable subscriptions |
| `jms.messagePrioritySupported` | pub hands messages on in arrival order |
| `jms.optimizeAcknowledge` | pub acknowledges each message |
| `jms.optimizeAcknowledgeTimeOut` | pub acknowledges each message |
| `jms.optimizedAckScheduledAckInterval` | pub acknowledges each message |
| `jms.consumerFailoverRedeliveryWaitPeriod` | pub does not fail over |

Destination options, passed through to the broker:

| Option | Applies to | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `producer.*` | send | ProducerInfo options: producer.windowSize, producer.dispatchAsync |
| `consumer.*` | receive | ConsumerInfo options, e.g. consumer.prefetchSize, consumer.selector |

## amqp module

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `broker-type` | choice | `auto` | servicebus = Azure Service Bus (browse by peeking; refuse selectors, move, --durable); auto = from the host name or the broker's container id |
| `client-id` | string | – | the AMQP container id; default: generated (durable subscriptions need a fixed one) |
| `vhost` | string | – | the hostname sent in SASL and open (virtual host; Azure/RabbitMQ use it); default: the URL host |
| `idle-timeout` | duration | `60s` | give up when the broker is silent this long; pub sends empty frames at half the broker's (0 = off) |
| `sasl-mechanisms` | string | – | SASL mechanisms in order of preference (PLAIN, ANONYMOUS, EXTERNAL); default: EXTERNAL with a client certificate, PLAIN with a user, else ANONYMOUS |
| `text-body` | choice | `value` | text bodies: value = amqp-value string (JMS TextMessage); data = data section with text/plain; charset=utf-8 |
| `credit` | count | `1000` | link credit for receiving (how many messages the broker may send ahead) |
| `prefetch-follows-count` | bool | `true` | grant only as much credit as -n asks for |

## ramqp module

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vhost` | string | `/` | the virtual host |
| `heartbeat` | duration | `60s` | heartbeat interval asked for (the smaller of ours and the broker's); 0 = the broker's |
| `confirms` | bool | `true` | publisher confirms: each send waits for the broker to take the message |
| `mandatory` | bool | – | a message nothing can route is an error (default: for queues yes, for exchanges no) |
| `prefetch` | count | `1000` | basic.qos prefetch count for receiving (1-65535) |
| `prefetch-follows-count` | bool | `true` | prefetch only as many messages as -n asks for |
| `sasl-mechanisms` | string | – | SASL mechanisms in order of preference (PLAIN, ANONYMOUS, EXTERNAL); default: EXTERNAL with a client certificate, PLAIN with a user, else ANONYMOUS |
| `exchange-type` | choice | `topic` | the type of exchange `pub dest create .../exchange/NAME` declares |
| `queue-type` | choice | – | x-queue-type for queues pub declares (dest create, durable subscriptions) |
| `connection-name` | string | – | a name for the connection in RabbitMQ's management UI |

## Message formats

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format.json.pretty` | bool | `false` | indent JSON output (one object per message, no longer one per line) |
| `format.json.body` | choice | `string` | auto: embed text bodies that are JSON as JSON values (not byte-exact); string: always a string |

## Configuration file

In the main `config` file only.

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `[core] default-scheme` | – | scheme for targets that are neither URLs nor aliases |
| `[core "config"] strict` | `true` | treat warnings as errors: unknown config keys/sections, message features the module cannot carry |
| `[core "config"] secret-file-max-mode` | `0400` | most permissive mode allowed on password-file (e.g. 0440 for group read) |
| `[core "config"] secret-file-check-owner` | `true` | require password-file to be owned by you |
| `[core "config"] secret-file-follow-symlinks` | `false` | accept password-file being a symbolic link |
| `[core "config"] tls-key-max-mode` | `0600` | most permissive mode allowed on the TLS private key file |
| `[core "config"] tls-key-check-owner` | `true` | require the TLS private key file to be owned by you |
| `[core "config"] tls-follow-symlinks` | `true` | accept cert, key and ca-file being symbolic links (cert-manager, certbot live/ paths) |
| `[core "config"] max-depth` | `16` | how deep config.d subdirectories are read (0 = flat); only honoured in the main config file |
| `[core "config"] check-permissions` | `true` | refuse config.d files/dirs writable by group or others, or not owned by you or root (main config only; PUB_CHECK_PERMISSIONS=false skips all) |
| `[core "config"] max-files` | `1024` | most config files under config.d (main config only) |
| `[core "config"] max-file-size` | `64k` | largest config file (main config only) |
| `[core "config"] max-total-size` | `4m` | most bytes of configuration in total (main config only) |
